name: Sextortion & Blackmail Scams
summary: A threat to publish intimate images, real or entirely invented, is used to extract escalating payments.

typicalLoss.note: Financial loss understates the harm. This scam causes severe psychological damage and has been linked to suicides worldwide.

targets: Teenagers and young men in particular
Anyone with a public social media presence

howItWorks.detail: An attractive stranger makes contact on Instagram, Snapchat, a dating app or Facebook, and moves quickly to intimate conversation and video.
The video call is recorded, or images are requested and saved. In many cases the other side is pre-recorded footage, not a live person.
Within minutes, contact turns to threat, usually with a screenshot of your friends list to show they know exactly who would receive it. A deadline of an hour or two is typical.

howItWorks.step: It never ends with one payment
howItWorks.detail: Paying confirms you can be pressured. Demands escalate. This is the single most important thing to understand about this scam.
Mass emails claim a device was hacked and a webcam recording exists, often quoting an old breached password as 'proof'. In these cases there is no footage at all.

redFlags: A new online contact who escalates to intimate video unusually fast.
They push to a platform where video can be recorded, and steer the conversation quickly.
An immediate threat with a short deadline and a demand in crypto, gift cards or e-wallet transfer.
An email quoting a password you recognise from years ago. That is from a public breach, not from your device.
Screenshots of your contact list presented as leverage.
illustrativeCase: A 19-year-old accepts an Instagram follow and moves to a video call that lasts under two minutes. Immediately afterwards he receives a recording of himself alongside a screenshot of his followers, including his mother and his employer, and a demand for R3 000 within one hour. He pays. The demand becomes R8 000. He pays again. It becomes R20 000.
howToProtect: Never share intimate images or perform on video with someone you have not met in person, however genuine they seem.
Lock down your friends and followers lists. Leverage in this scam comes from visible contacts.
Understand in advance that paying makes it worse, not better. Decide this now, not in the panic.
Talk to young people about it directly and without judgement, so that if it happens they come to you instead of paying alone.
Ignore mass blackmail emails quoting an old password, and change that password wherever it is still used.
ifYouveBeenHit: Do not pay. Paying does not end it and funds further attempts.
Stop responding entirely and do not delete anything. Screenshot the profile, the threats and any payment details.
Report and block the account on the platform. Major platforms have dedicated sextortion reporting routes and act quickly.
Open a SAPS case. Extortion is a serious criminal offence in South Africa.
Tell someone you trust. Isolation is the entire leverage, and removing the secret removes the threat's power. Free counselling is available through the SADAG helpline.

faqs.q: Will they really send it to my contacts?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but far less often than threatened, and much less often once you stop responding. These are volume operations that move on to people who engage.

faqs.q: An email says my webcam was hacked and quotes my password.
faqs.a: That password came from a public data breach, and in essentially all such cases there is no recording. Delete the email and change the password anywhere it is still in use.

faqs.q: I am a minor and this happened to me.
faqs.a: Tell a trusted adult immediately. You are the victim of a crime and you are not in trouble. Report it to the SAPS and to the platform, and do not pay.
